item.title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mptcp: do not use Fast Open...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child. MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs. [ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]
Suggested next step: Check whether the named product and affected versions are in use; follow the original vendor's remediation guidance.
Original advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pmjw-rj44-w725

item.title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ceph: clamp the inline data...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data() The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need() only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes. ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end. Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant() and fill_inode(), are covered.
Suggested next step: Check whether the named product and affected versions are in use; follow the original vendor's remediation guidance.
Original advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55q4-ccgm-63vh

item.title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.3 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as potentially malicious. hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too: the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than the ring. The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices, hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO. One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch: hv_g

Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). item.title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
NFSD: copy SETXATTR data...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.4 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: copy SETXATTR data from all XDR buffer segments nfsd4_vbuf_from_vector() manually copies the head followed by whole pages starting at offset zero. This assumes that all remaining data starts at the beginning of the page array and that no data is stored in the tail. However, nfsd4_decode_setxattr() passes an xdr_buf returned by xdr_stream_subsegment(). Such a sub-buffer can have a nonzero page_base and can span its page and tail segments. Ignoring that layout can copy the wrong bytes into the value passed to vfs_setxattr(). Use read_bytes_from_xdr_buf(), which observes the complete xdr_buf layout.
Suggested next step: Check whether the named product and affected versions are in use; follow the original vendor's remediation guidance.

item.title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfs: mark the inode...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.4 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them. Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

xfs: refuse a pNFS...
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.4 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data. Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Consolidate implementations of refcount_t"), default builds implemented refcount_inc_not_zero() using atomic_add_unless(), which provided full memory ordering on success. Use acquire ordering when it takes its own reference for a refcounted socket. Use refcount_set_release() when setting refcounts in the SYN cookie, TCP F

item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix buffer overflow in SMB2_tcon() In SMB2_tcon(), unc_path is allocated with a fixed buffer size of MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH * 2 bytes (672 bytes). However, the user-controlled UNC path (tree) length is passed to cifs_strtoUTF16(), which assumes the destination buffer is large enough and writes strlen(tree) + 1 UTF-16 code units. Commit 62a1a439e0fd ("cifs: clean up handling of unc= option") removed the length check on UNC mount options, allowing mount paths to exceed MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH while retaining the fixed-size buffer allocation in SMB2_tcon(). Consequently, an oversized UNC string causes cifs_strtoUTF16() to write past the end of the heap object, resulting in a slab-out-of-bounds write. Furthermore, if a tree exceeds MAX_TREE_SIZE characters, strscpy() truncates it in cifs_tcon::tree_name, causing subs
Suggested next step: Check whether the named product and affected versions are in use; follow the original vendor's remediation guidance.

The test in nfsd4_sequence_done() therefore no longer identifies a replay, and every replay now stores its reply and clears NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE as though it owned the slot. item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: Do not credit control-record octets to the RPC stream svc_tcp_sock_recv_cmsg() receives up to two octets into a local buffer, and returns that count for any record type other than TLS_RECORD_TYPE_ALERT. Nothing reached the caller's buffer, but svc_tcp_read_marker() adds the count to sk_tcplen and svc_tcp_read_msg()'s caller adds it to sk_datalen. The RPC stream advances over octets it never received. The fragment marker is assembled from stale sk_marker octets. The message body comes from pages nothing wrote. A conforming client reaches this. Each pair is credited the same way. Retu

item.title: Red Hat Quay security advisory CVE-2026-123710
item.description:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.
Suggested next step: Review the original advisory and affected build or distribution components. Verify upstream status before changing dependencies.

item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 8.2 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Description ### Summary On a self-hosted, single-tenant Budibase instance (`multiTenancy:false`), the public bootstrap endpoint `POST /api/global/users/init` remains fully exploitable **after** the instance has been provisioned. item.title: Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.7 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Description ### Summary A **low-privileged application end-user** (role `BASIC` - **not** a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a **builder or admin** later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section **Formula** column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as **raw HTML** and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin. The Builder SPA is served by nginx with **no Content-Security-Policy** (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered *published-app* document, not `/builder/`). item.title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: # Summary `svg2rlg()` expands `<use>` references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (`CircularRefError`). A group containing N `<use>` elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10. item.description:

Summary: ### Summary A remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability, allows any remote client to cause a complete crash of the Aedes MQTT broker process. item.title: appium allows unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion in @appium/storage-plugin
item.description:

item.title: Traefik versions >= v3.7.0 and < v3.7.11 contain an authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider. The TLS option generated for an In
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 8.2
Summary: Traefik versions >= v3.7.0 and < v3.7.11 contain an authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider. The TLS option generated for an Ingress carrying the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret annotation was named after the Ingress namespace and name. As a result, two Ingress objects sharing the same host, the same client CA secret, and the same client-authentication mode produced two distinct TLS option names for that host. Traefik treats this as a TLS options conflict and falls back to the entry point's default TLS configuration, which does not request a client certificate, so a route configured with nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on" becomes reachable without a client certificate. Only the v3.7 line is affected; the issue is fixed in v3.7.11.

item.title: Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex
item.description:
Severity: HIGH
Summary: ### Impact `Schema.TemplateLiteral` compiles each `Schema.String` span to the lazy wildcard `[\s\S]*?` and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more `Schema.String` spans, for example: ```ts Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X") ``` the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. A 5,000-character string of `:` characters blocks the event loop for about 15 seconds. Applications that decode untrusted input with such a schema are affected. That includes `Schema.decodeUnknown`, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.is`, and anything built on them, such as `HttpApi` request payloads and `@effect/rpc` payloads. ### Patches Fixed in `effect@3.22.1` (#6
